title: Define the MVP and record client-side platform access
body:
Goal: the agreed MVP scope and the architecture change are written down before the M2 roadmap.
Acceptance: `docs/milestone2-mvp.md` holds decisions D1-D24, the MAL API findings and the Google sign-in and Play findings; `docs/future-features.md` lists the parked ideas with the decision each came from; ADR 0007 (client-side platform access) is accepted and listed in `docs/decisions/README.md` and the root README; CLAUDE.md and the README replace the rule that only the server talks to MAL (module list, architecture diagram, Auth section); `docs/tickets-m2.csv` holds the M2 prep tickets; relative links resolve.
Out of scope: skill changes (M2-0c), agent changes (M2-0a, M2-0b), the M2 roadmap.
Skill: adr, ticket-workflow.

title: Rewrite the existing agents with project knowledge
body:
Goal: the six agents in `.claude/agents/` know this project, so the main session gets useful, compact output instead of generic answers.
Acceptance: every agent has a `description` saying when to use it, `tools`, `model`, `skills:` (only skills it needs on every call), a body with the project facts it cannot guess, a fixed report format, and the hard rules (no commits or pushes, `git add` new files, never spawn agents, stay in the given scope). Per agent:
- `Explore` (haiku; Read, Grep, Glob; skill codebase-overview): module map, package convention `com.greenzean.animekmp.<module>.<feature>`, where the SDL, SQLDelight `.sq` files, Flyway migrations, Koin modules and ADRs live. Answer: a direct answer, then at most ~15 `path:line` hits, no file dumps, a plain not found when nothing matches.
- `build-runner` (haiku; Bash, Read): command table matching CI (lint `./gradlew spotlessCheck detekt`; Android `./gradlew :androidApp:assembleDebug :shared:allTests`; server `./gradlew :server:build`, which needs Docker for Testcontainers, say so if it is down; schema `./gradlew :server:test -PupdateSchema`). Plain `./gradlew` commands without pipes so the gradle-filter hook trims output. On failure, read `build/reports/tests/` or the detekt reports for the cause. Report PASS/FAIL per task, then per failure the task, test, `file:line`, a 1-3 line error and the likely cause. Never edit files or run `spotlessApply` unless asked.
- `docs` (haiku; Read, Write, Edit; skills adr, ticket-workflow): doc types and their formats: ADRs (template, numbering, index and README links, status), ticket text (Goal, Depends on, Acceptance, Out of scope, Skill; CSV columns as in `docs/tickets-m0-m1.csv`), README sections, `docs/milestone2-mvp.md` and `docs/future-features.md` (D-numbers). Short sentences, tables for comparisons. Never invent decisions, versions or URLs; list gaps under Missing.
- `researcher` (sonnet; Read, WebSearch, WebFetch): stack context (KMP/CMP, AGP 9, Ktor, graphql-kotlin, Apollo Kotlin, SQLDelight, Koin, Exposed, Flyway, Postgres, MAL API v2, Google Credential Manager). Source priority: official docs and release notes, then Maven Central or Google Maven, then GitHub releases; blogs never as the primary source. Versions: newest stable at least two weeks old, with its release date. Output per question: answer, URL, checked date, confidence (read directly, from a summary, unverified), ready to paste into an ADR Context.
- `reviewer` (opus, high; Read, Grep, Glob, Bash; skills ticket-workflow, codebase-overview): steps `gh issue view <n>`, `git diff main...HEAD` plus uncommitted changes, check every acceptance criterion and out-of-scope item; check the CLAUDE.md code rules, ADR 0007, scope to the named modules, tests in `commonTest` and the server, SDL committed and in sync, ADR written when a decision changed. Output: verdict, criteria checklist (met, not met, not verifiable), findings by severity with `path:line`. Bash only for read-only git and gh.
- `security-reviewer` (opus, high; Read, Grep, Glob; skill sync-protocol): threat model for this repo: public repo and untrusted client; ADR 0007 (MAL tokens only on the device in Keystore-backed storage, no platform tokens or platform user data on the server); Google ID token checks (signature, `aud` = web client ID, `iss`, `exp`, nonce, users keyed on `sub`); our session tokens; per-user authorization in every resolver (user ID from the token, never from input); GraphQL depth, complexity and batch-size limits; `pushChanges` input validation; secrets, `.env` and keystores; CI on fork PRs; MAL agreement limits (no stored credentials, privacy policy); Play account deletion. Output: findings with severity, `path:line`, exploit scenario and fix.
Verified: every frontmatter parses, tool names exist and each `skills:` entry matches a folder in `.claude/skills/`; smoke runs of `Explore` (where is the pull cursor stored?), `build-runner` (lint only) and `docs` (format a one-line test ticket without writing a file) follow their report formats.
Out of scope: new agents (M2-0b), changes to skills, settings or hooks.
Skill: ticket-workflow.

title: Create the area agents
body:
Goal: the area agents planned in CLAUDE.md exist, so large M2 features can be split by module.
Depends on: M2-0a (reuses its hard rules and report format).
Acceptance: five agents, all sonnet with tools Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, Bash. Common body: implement only the given part of a ticket inside the agent's module(s) and report anything outside instead of changing it; follow the preloaded skills and the ADRs; run the module's tests and `./gradlew spotlessCheck detekt` itself with plain `./gradlew` (subagents cannot call build-runner); `git add` new files; no commits or pushes; never spawn agents. Report: files changed, tests run and their result, deviations from the plan, open questions. Per agent:
- `server` (skills ktor-server-conventions, postgres-migrations, graphql-schema, sync-protocol): `server/` only. Schema changes go server first; the SDL is regenerated with `./gradlew :server:test -PupdateSchema`, never edited by hand. Never calls MAL (ADR 0007). Tests: `:server:test`.
- `shared-kmp` (skills kmp-data-layer, kmp-error-handling, kmp-di-koin, sync-protocol, graphql-schema): `shared/` (`commonMain` and platform `actual`s), plus `androidApp/` only for platform wiring such as WorkManager. The MAL client lives here, with tokens behind a secure-storage interface. Tests: `:shared:allTests`.
- `compose-ui` (skills kmp-compose-ui, kmp-presentation-mvi, kmp-navigation): `composeApp/` only. Uses the view model interface it is given and reports needed view model changes instead of making them. Previews and accessibility. Build: `:androidApp:assembleDebug`.
- `tester` (skills kmp-testing, postgres-migrations): writes and fixes tests only (`commonTest`, `server/src/test`); fakes over mocks, Testcontainers for the database. Does not change production code; reports bugs it finds.
- `build-ci` (skill kmp-module-structure): `gradle/libs.versions.toml`, the `build.gradle.kts` files, `.github/workflows/`, `config/detekt`, `.editorconfig`, `docker-compose.yml`, `Dockerfile`. Every version change comes with a source and release date; no secrets in workflows; fork PRs get no secrets.
- `CLAUDE.md` Delegation updated: the area agents exist; keep only for large features and the feature order; add that area agents run their own Gradle checks.
Verified: every frontmatter parses, tool names exist and each `skills:` entry matches a folder in `.claude/skills/`; after a session restart `/agents` lists all 11 project agents.
Out of scope: changes to the existing six agents (M2-0a), skills, settings or hooks.
Skill: ticket-workflow, kmp-module-structure.

title: Align skills with ADR 0007
body:
Goal: the skills stop saying that the server talks to MAL, matching ADR 0007.
Depends on: M2-0 (ADR 0007).
Acceptance: `codebase-overview`: `shared/` lists the MAL client and says only the app talks to MAL; `server/` says it syncs libraries between a user's devices, never calls MAL and stores no platform tokens, platform user data or anime metadata; `docs/` mentions `milestone2-mvp.md`. `kmp-module-structure`: the module tree shows the MAL client in `shared/` and no MAL adapter in `server/`. `ktor-server-conventions`: the intro rule matches ADR 0007, and the not-decided-yet note names auth (Google ID token verification, session tokens) instead of the MAL adapter. `grep -rn 'MAL adapter\|talks to MAL' .claude/` finds no old-rule text.
Out of scope: agents (M2-0a, M2-0b), other skills.
Skill: codebase-overview, kmp-module-structure, ktor-server-conventions.

title: Write the M2 roadmap
body:
Goal: the MVP decisions D1-D24 are split into ordered tickets with dependencies.
Acceptance: `docs/m2-roadmap.md` lists the tickets in order with dependencies and the D-numbers each covers; every D-number maps to at least one ticket; the tickets are rows in `docs/tickets-m2.csv`; relative links resolve.
Out of scope: creating the GitHub issues, any code.
Skill: ticket-workflow.

title: Spike: MAL API with a real client ID
body:
Goal: replace the unconfirmed MAL API points with tested facts. Time-box 1 to 2 days.
Depends on: a MAL client ID registered by the user.
Acceptance: tested with a real client ID: search and details with only `X-MAL-CLIENT-ID`; the `recommendations` field on details (shape, size); `/anime/suggestions` response shape and the empty list for new users; rate-limit behaviour and the 403 block; which app type MAL offers when registering and whether PKCE `plain` works without a secret; list read and write (`/users/@me/animelist`); decision in `docs/decisions/0008-mal-api.md` (caching, backoff, fields to request); `docs/milestone2-mvp.md` findings updated.
Out of scope: production MAL client code.
Covers: D5, D10, D11, D13, D14. Skill: adr.

title: Server stores IDs only: drop the dev catalog
body:
Goal: the server holds library entries and anime IDs, not anime details (ADR 0007).
Depends on: M2-2.
Acceptance: decision on entries referencing `mal_id` directly or the `anime` table becoming an ID map, written in an ADR; Flyway migration drops `title` and any other anime detail from the server; the debug dev catalog is removed; the SDL is regenerated and committed; the client sync path follows the new shape; sync tests and the Testcontainers migration test pass; existing local libraries still sync.
Out of scope: accounts (M2-4).
Covers: D2, D19. Skills: sync-protocol, postgres-migrations, graphql-schema, adr.

title: Server: Google sign-in and session tokens
body:
Goal: the server accepts a Google ID token and issues its own session token.
Depends on: M2-3.
Acceptance: `signInWithGoogle` mutation; ID token checked for signature (Google's rotating keys), `aud` = web client ID, `iss`, `exp` and nonce; users table keyed on `sub`, no email used as the key; session token (short-lived access plus refresh) signed with a secret from env; token and client ID config in `.env.example`; tests with a fake key set for each check that must fail; SDL committed.
Out of scope: the Android sign-in UI (M2-6), authorizing sync (M2-5).
Covers: D24. Skills: graphql-schema, ktor-server-conventions, postgres-migrations.

title: Server: authorize sync per user
body:
Goal: every sync operation runs as the signed-in user; the hardcoded dev user is gone.
Depends on: M2-4.
Acceptance: `pushChanges` and `changesSince` read the user ID from the session token, never from input; entries of one user are never visible to another (tests with two users); unauthenticated calls are rejected with a typed error; the client sends the session token and refreshes it on expiry; dev user removed from server and client.
Out of scope: the sign-in UI (M2-6).
Covers: D2, D24. Skills: sync-protocol, graphql-schema.

title: App: Google sign-in and optional account
body:
Goal: the user can sign in with Google; the app still works fully without an account.
Depends on: M2-4.
Acceptance: Credential Manager with the Sign in with Google library behind an interface (`expect/actual` or Android-only implementation in `androidApp`); versions rechecked on Maven; ID token sent to `signInWithGoogle`; session token in Keystore-backed secure storage; account state in a view model (signed out / signed in); sign-in screen reachable from settings, never required to use the app; view model tests with fakes.
Out of scope: merging the local library (M2-7), account deletion (M2-8).
Covers: D1, D24. Skills: kmp-presentation-mvi, kmp-data-layer, kmp-di-koin.

title: First login merge and logout choice
body:
Goal: signing in does not lose data and signing out lets the user decide.
Depends on: M2-5, M2-6.
Acceptance: on first login on a device with a library, its entries are merged into the account automatically (pending changes pushed, account entries pulled, last-write-wins as in ADR 0006); on logout the app asks whether to keep or delete the library on the device; tests for both paths including a library with entries on two devices.
Out of scope: MAL linking (M2-21).
Covers: D18, D20. Skill: sync-protocol.

title: Account deletion in the app and on the web
body:
Goal: meet the Play account-deletion policy.
Depends on: M2-5, M2-6.
Acceptance: `deleteAccount` mutation removes the user, entries and tombstones in one transaction; in-app delete flow with confirmation; a public web page (served by the server) explains and starts deletion; declared in the Data safety form notes; data kept for security or legal reasons is listed; server test proves nothing remains for the user.
Out of scope: the Play listing (M2-26).
Covers: D22. Skills: graphql-schema, postgres-migrations.

title: App: MAL login with PKCE
body:
Goal: the user can log in to MAL on this device and the app keeps the tokens safely.
Depends on: M2-2.
Acceptance: authorization code with PKCE (`plain`), no client secret; browser redirect handled behind an interface; access and refresh tokens in Keystore-backed storage, never sent to our server; refresh on expiry; logout deletes the tokens; MAL client ID read from config (public); typed errors; tests with a fake MAL server (Ktor MockEngine).
Out of scope: using the tokens for list sync (M2-17, M2-19).
Covers: D1, D3, D4. Skills: kmp-data-layer, kmp-error-handling, kmp-di-koin.

title: App: MAL search and details with cache and backoff
body:
Goal: search for anime and load details through MAL, cached on the device.
Depends on: M2-2.
Acceptance: Ktor MAL client with the `X-MAL-CLIENT-ID` header; search and details calls with the fields chosen in ADR 0008; results cached in SQLDelight with an expiry (client-side caching only as long as reasonably necessary); backoff and stop on HTTP 403; offline returns a typed `NoConnection` error; tests with MockEngine and an in-memory database.
Out of scope: screens (M2-11).
Covers: D5, D10. Skills: kmp-data-layer, kmp-error-handling.

title: Rework the M2 tickets
body:
**Goal:** the remaining M2 tickets are usable features, in work order, with plain titles and no open questions.

**Where in the app:** nowhere. Tickets, docs and process only.

**Acceptance:**
- Old open tickets #63-#79 closed as "not planned", each pointing to its replacement. New tickets #109-#126 (M2-11..M2-27, M2-31), numbered in work order and depending only on lower numbers.
- Each new ticket says where the user reaches it in the app, has a Contract (State, Action, Event, SDL) and a Decisions section.
- `docs/m2-roadmap.md` and `docs/tickets-m2.csv` match the new tickets. `docs/milestone2-mvp.md` gains D25-D27 and the strict D17 note.
- Old ticket numbers in ADRs 0008, 0009, 0013, 0014, `docs/data-safety.md` and the postgres-migrations skill are updated.
- Process: CLAUDE.md and the `ticket-workflow` skill require usable tickets, plain titles and up-front decisions, and run back end and views in parallel. The `shared-kmp` and `compose-ui` agents are set up for parallel work against the Contract. The Definition of Done holds the design criteria.

**Decisions:**
- Navigation is a bottom bar (Library, Search, For you), with Settings in the Library top bar.
- Titles are English by default, with a Settings option (D25). Status follows progress like on MAL (D26). Connecting MAL merges both ways (D27).
- D17 stays strict: changes made on a device without MAL never reach MAL.
- The host is chosen in M2-25, before Play (M2-27). The privacy contact is a dedicated address from the user. The user already has a Play developer account.

**Depends on:** M2-10.
**Out of scope:** code changes.

title: Add anime from MAL search
body:
**Goal:** the user finds an anime on MyAnimeList and adds it to their library.

**Where in the app:** a new bottom bar with **Library**, **Search** and **For you** (a "coming soon" placeholder until M2-16). Settings stays as an icon in the Library top bar. In Search, type a title and tap **Add** on a result.

**Contract** (fixed in the plan, before work starts):
- `SearchState(query, results: List<SearchResultUi>, status)`, where status is Idle, Loading, Results, Empty, Offline or Error
- `SearchResultUi(malId, title, imageUrl, inLibrary)`
- Actions: `OnQueryChange(text)`, `OnAddClick(malId)`, `OnRetryClick`

**Acceptance:**
- Search uses the existing `MalAnimeRepository`, which needs no MAL login (client ID only). Typing is debounced.
- Add saves the entry (status Plan to watch), the anime's title and its image URL locally. The result then shows "In library".
- An entry synced from another device, for an anime this device has not seen yet, gets its title and image from MAL.
- Offline, the screen says that searching needs a connection. The library keeps working.
- The dev seed list is gone (`DevAnimeSeed` and the "addable" list on the library screen).
- Library rows show the cover image.
- Settings › Display › **Title language**: English (default) or Main title.
- View model tests for every status.

**Depends on:** nothing open.
**Out of scope:** the details screen (M2-12) and searching your own library (M2-14).

**Decisions** (made when the ticket was written; ask only if the code contradicts them):
- The bottom bar is built once here, with all three tabs.
- `anime` gets `title_en` and `image_url` (SQLDelight migration). MAL fields include `alternative_titles`.
- Title language is stored on the device only. English falls back to the main title when MAL has no English title.
- Search starts at 3 characters (MAL's minimum), with a 400 ms debounce. Pages of 20, more on scroll, `nsfw=false`.
- A new entry starts as Plan to watch.
- Rows waiting in `parked_change` (#41) are resolved by fetching the title and image from MAL details. Seeded anime rows already on devices stay. The seed code is deleted.
- Images use Coil 3 with the Ktor engine. Check the latest stable version with a search.

title: Anime details screen
body:
**Goal:** the user sees what an anime is about, before or after adding it.

**Where in the app:** tap a result in Search or an entry in Library.

**Contract:**
- `DetailsState(details: AnimeDetailsUi?, inLibrary, status)`, where status is Loading, Loaded, Offline or Error
- `AnimeDetailsUi(malId, title, imageUrl, synopsis, episodes, meanScore, genres, airingStatus)`
- Actions: `OnAddClick`, `OnRetryClick`, `OnBackClick`

**Acceptance:**
- Uses the existing `MalAnimeRepository.details`, with its cache. No MAL login.
- Offline, it shows the cached details, or says a connection is needed when there are none.
- **Add** works the same way as in Search.
- A type-safe route that takes the MAL ID.
- View model tests for every status.

**Depends on:** M2-11.
**Out of scope:** editing the entry (M2-13) and per-anime recommendations.

**Decisions** (made when the ticket was written; ask only if the code contradicts them):
- Fields: cover, title in the chosen language with the other title below it, synopsis, episodes, airing status, MAL mean score, genres, start date.
- A **View on MyAnimeList** link opens the browser, for attribution.
- Offline with nothing cached: the same offline view as Search. Cache rules: the existing `MalAnimeRepository` ones.

title: Check DI graph and view models
body:
**Goal:** a wrong view model dependency or a broken Koin wiring fails the build, not the emulator check.

**Where in the app:** nowhere (tests only).

**Acceptance:**
- A Koin graph test in `shared` builds the full module list and fails when a definition cannot be resolved, including the use cases and `parametersOf(malId)` for the details view model.
- A Konsist rule fails the build when a `*ViewModel` constructor takes a `*Repository` or a `*DataSource`. It runs in `:shared:allTests`, so CI enforces it.
- Break each check once and see it fail.
- The `kmp-di-koin` and `kmp-testing` skills mention both checks.

**Depends on:** M2-12.

**Out of scope:** other architecture rules (package dependencies, naming).

**Decisions** (made when the ticket was written; ask only if the code contradicts them):
- Konsist is the tool for the view model rule; check library version and KMP support with a search before adding it.
- The Koin test uses `verify()` or `checkModules` if it supports the KMP setup; otherwise a test that resolves every view model.

title: Test Settings and For you screens
body:
**Goal:** the Settings and For you screens have the same view tests as Search, Library and Details.

**Where in the app:** nowhere (tests only).

**Acceptance:**
- `runComposeUiTest` tests in `composeApp/src/androidHostTest` for Settings (including the Display settings screen) and For you, as the `kmp-testing` skill describes: every state, every action, accessibility labels, UX rules, 48dp touch targets.
- Robot pattern, one robot per screen.
- Break each behavior once and see a test fail.
- A bug found while testing is fixed in this ticket if it is small, otherwise a new ticket.

**Depends on:** M2-12.

**Out of scope:** new screens or visual changes.

**Decisions** (made when the ticket was written; ask only if the code contradicts them):
- Test the stateless `Screen(state, onAction)` composables only. Roots stay covered by the view model tests.

title: Move texts to string resources
body:
**Goal:** all texts of the app come from string resources, so the app can be translated later and the code has no text literals.

**Where in the app:** every screen (no visible change in English).

**Contract:** `UiText` (a string resource with arguments, or a plain string) in `composeApp` (`shared` cannot reach the resources) for texts built from typed state, such as error messages. View models keep typed state: statuses, errors and a `MalDate` instead of formatted dates.

**Acceptance:**
- Every user-visible string in `composeApp` and in the `shared` mappers is a string resource, including `contentDescription` values.
- View model states hold typed values (errors, statuses, `MalDate`) instead of formatted English strings; `composeApp` maps them to `UiText`.
- The MAL "not found" and "throttled" errors on the details screen show their own clear message instead of the generic one.
- `@Stable` or immutable collections on the states that hold lists, if the compiler report shows they are unstable.
- Existing view and view model tests pass, reading the texts from the resources.
- Emulator check of every screen; no visible change in English.

**Depends on:** M2-12.

**Out of scope:** adding a second language.

**Decisions** (made when the ticket was written; ask only if the code contradicts them):
- Compose Multiplatform resources (`Res.string`) are used, as the skill describes. Verify support in the current version before starting.
- Do this before M2-13, so the new editing screens start with resources.

title: Track status, episodes and score
body:
**Goal:** the user records where they are in an anime and what they think of it.

**Where in the app:** on the details screen of an anime that is in the library: a status selector, episodes watched with + and −, a score from 1 to 10 (or none), and **Remove from library**. Library rows show status, progress, score and sync state.

**Contract** (server first):
- SDL: `progress: Int!` and `score: Int` on the list entry in the push and pull operations
- `EntryEditUi(status, progress, totalEpisodes, score)`
- Actions: `OnStatusChange`, `OnProgressChange`, `OnScoreChange`, `OnRemoveClick`

**Acceptance:**
- Server: a Flyway migration adds progress and score. `pushChanges` rejects a score outside 1-10 and a negative progress. SDL committed, server tests pass.
- App: a SQLDelight migration. Sync sends and receives the new fields. The same validation runs in the app, and progress cannot go past the episode count when it is known.
- Remove creates a tombstone that syncs.
- Tests: server validation, a sync round trip, the view model.

**Order inside the ticket:** server and SDL first, then shared and composeApp in parallel.
**Depends on:** M2-12.
**Out of scope:** dates, rewatch count and notes.

**Decisions** (made when the ticket was written; ask only if the code contradicts them):
- Automatic status, like MAL: progress above 0 on Plan to watch sets Watching. Progress reaching the episode total sets Completed. Choosing Completed sets progress to the total, when it is known.
- Score: a 1-10 selector plus "No score". Progress: + and −, or tap the number to type it.
- Library rows with status Watching get a **+1** button.
- Remove has no dialog. A snackbar offers **Undo**.
- The server keeps last-write-wins on the whole entry. No per-field merge.
- Server limits: progress 0-10000 (the server does not know the total), score 1-10 or null.

title: Search, filter and sort your library
body:
**Goal:** the user finds entries in their own library, offline.

**Where in the app:** the library screen: a search field, status filter chips and a sort menu.

**Contract:**
- `LibraryState` gets `query`, `statusFilter: WatchStatus?` and `sort` (Title, Score or LastUpdated)
- Actions: `OnQueryChange`, `OnStatusFilterClick`, `OnSortChange`

**Acceptance:**
- SQLDelight queries do the search, filter and sort. Removed entries never show.
- "No results" looks different from "your library is empty".
- Tests with an in-memory database, plus view model tests.

**Depends on:** M2-13 (sort by score).
**Out of scope:** filters by genre, year or type.

**Decisions** (made when the ticket was written; ask only if the code contradicts them):
- The status filter is single select: All plus the five statuses, like MAL's tabs.
- Sort: Last updated (default, newest first), Title, Score (unscored last). The sort is remembered on the device; the query is not.
- Search matches the English and main titles, case-insensitive.

title: Connect your MAL account
body:
**Goal:** the user links their MyAnimeList account on this device.

**Where in the app:** a new **MyAnimeList** section in Settings.

**Contract:**
- `MalAccountState(status)`, where status is NotConnected, Connecting, Connected or Error(reason)
- Actions: `OnConnectClick`, `OnDisconnectClick`

**Acceptance:**
- Before connecting, the section explains what the app does with MAL (reads and updates your list on this device, nothing is stored on our server), and the user agrees. The MAL agreement requires this consent.
- **Connect** runs the existing `MalAuthManager.login()` (PKCE in a browser tab).
- Cancelled, denied and network errors each get a clear message.
- **Disconnect** clears the tokens and the MAL cache.
- The state survives an app restart.
- View model tests for every status.

**Depends on:** nothing open. Can be done at any point.
**Out of scope:** the privacy policy page (M2-26 adds the link).

**Decisions** (made when the ticket was written; ask only if the code contradicts them):
- The consent is shown once, before the first connect, and stored on the device. It is shown again after Disconnect.
- Connected state shows the MAL username from `GET /users/@me`, stored on the device only.
- **Merge on connect:** connecting starts the MAL import (M2-20) and the upload of app-only entries (M2-21). Those tickets add the hook; until they exist, this only connects.
- Disconnect clears tokens, the username and the MAL cache. The library stays.

title: Suggestions from MAL
body:
**Goal:** the user gets MAL's personal suggestions and adds the ones they like.

**Where in the app:** a **For you** tab in the bottom bar.

**Contract:**
- `SuggestionsState(items: List<SearchResultUi>, status)`, where status is NotConnected, Loading, Loaded, Empty, Offline or Error
- Actions: `OnConnectClick`, `OnAddClick(malId)`, `OnItemClick(malId)`, `OnRetryClick`

**Acceptance:**
- Calls `GET /anime/suggestions` with the user's token, cached and throttled like search.
- Not connected: the tab explains why and shows a **Connect MAL** button (the M2-15 flow).
- Empty: the tab explains that MAL needs some rated anime first.
- Cards look like the search results. **Add** works, and tapping a card opens the details screen.
- MockEngine tests for the call, plus view model tests.

**Depends on:** M2-12, M2-15.
**Out of scope:** per-anime recommendations.

**Decisions** (made when the ticket was written; ask only if the code contradicts them):
- Replaces the "coming soon" placeholder in the For you tab.
- Pages of 20 with load more, up to MAL's 100.
- Anime already in the library are hidden.
- Refreshed when the tab opens if the cache is older than 1 day.

title: Export your library to a MAL file
body:
**Goal:** the user saves their library as a file MyAnimeList can import.

**Where in the app:** Settings › Library › **Export to MAL file**.

**Contract:**
- `ExportState(status)`, where status is Idle, Exporting, Done(count) or Error
- Actions: `OnExportClick`, `OnFileChosen`

**Acceptance:**
- A writer for MAL's XML export format, with status, progress and score for each entry.
- The Android save dialog sits behind an interface.
- Tests on the XML output.

**Depends on:** M2-13.
**Out of scope:** CSV or JSON.

**Decisions** (made when the ticket was written; ask only if the code contradicts them):
- Plain XML (no gzip), file name `animekmp-mal-export-YYYY-MM-DD.xml`.
- A minimal `<myinfo>` with counts. `update_on_import` is set to 1.
- Removed entries are not exported.
- Manual check: import the file on a MAL test account and note the result in the PR.

title: Import a MAL export file
body:
**Goal:** the user brings in a list exported from MyAnimeList, with no login.

**Where in the app:** Settings › Library › **Import MAL file**.

**Contract:**
- `ImportFileState(status)`, where status is Idle, Importing(progress), Done(added, keptYours, invalid) or Error
- Actions: `OnImportClick`, `OnFileChosen`

**Acceptance:**
- The file picker sits behind an interface.
- The parser reads MAL's XML, plain or gzip.
- New entries are added.
- For entries that are already in the library but differ, the app's version is kept and counted in the summary. M2-19 turns these into choices for the user.
- Tests on a sample file, plus a round trip: export with M2-17, import, get the same entries.

**Depends on:** M2-17.
**Out of scope:** importing through a MAL login (M2-20).

**Decisions** (made when the ticket was written; ask only if the code contradicts them):
- Accepts `.xml` and `.xml.gz`.
- For anime not on the device, an `anime` row is made from the file's title, and the image is fetched like parked rows (M2-11).
- Equal entries are skipped. Differing entries, including ones removed in the app, keep the app's version and count as "kept yours".
- Imported entries are local changes, so they sync to our server, and to MAL once M2-21 exists.
- Invalid rows (unknown status, missing ID) are counted and skipped.

title: Choose which version to keep
body:
**Goal:** when the app and MyAnimeList disagree about an anime, the user picks which version to keep.

**Where in the app:** a banner on the library ("N anime need your choice") and a row in Settings open the **conflicts** screen.

**Contract:**
- `ConflictsState(items: List<ConflictUi>)`, with `ConflictUi(malId, title, app: EntryValues, mal: EntryValues)`
- Actions: `OnKeepAppClick(malId)`, `OnKeepMalClick(malId)`, `OnKeepAllAppClick`, `OnKeepAllMalClick`

**Acceptance:**
- An ADR (next free number) states what counts as a conflict (same anime, different status, progress or score), where open conflicts are stored, and that a choice is an ordinary local change that syncs to our server.
- Conflicts are stored locally and survive a restart.
- File import (M2-18) now creates conflicts instead of silently keeping the app's version.
- Each conflict shows both versions side by side. There is a "nothing to resolve" state.
- Tests: keep app, keep MAL, and keep all.

**Depends on:** M2-18.
**Out of scope:** conflicts from MAL account import and from MAL sync. M2-20 and M2-22 reuse this screen.

**Decisions** (made when the ticket was written; ask only if the code contradicts them):
- A conflict means the same MAL ID with a different status, progress, score or removed state.
- While a conflict waits, the entry keeps the app's version and syncs normally. The other version is stored in a `conflict` table.
- Keep app: delete the conflict. Keep other: write it as a new local change, then delete the conflict.
- Every difference is a conflict, with no automatic newest-wins (D15).
- The banner cannot be dismissed while conflicts exist. A new import replaces an older conflict for the same anime.

title: Import your list from MAL
body:
**Goal:** a user connected to MyAnimeList pulls their MAL list into the app.

**Where in the app:** Settings › MyAnimeList › **Import my MAL list**, shown while connected.

**Contract:**
- `MalImportState(status)`, where status is Idle, Importing(done, total), Done(added, conflicts) or Error
- Actions: `OnImportClick`, `OnRetryClick`

**Acceptance:**
- A paged read of `/users/@me/animelist` with the list status, through the existing throttle and backoff.
- New entries are added. Differences become conflicts (M2-19).
- After a failure, the import resumes where it stopped.
- MockEngine tests, plus view model tests.

**Depends on:** M2-15, M2-19.
**Out of scope:** ongoing sync (M2-21, M2-22).

**Decisions** (made when the ticket was written; ask only if the code contradicts them):
- Runs automatically right after connecting MAL (merge on connect), and also from the button.
- Pages of 100 through `MalThrottle`. The stored offset lets it resume after a failure.
- Anime that exist only in the app are left for M2-21.
- Imported entries are marked `on_mal`, which M2-22 needs to detect removals on MAL.

title: Send your changes to MAL
body:
**Goal:** changes made in the app show up on MyAnimeList automatically.

**Where in the app:** this runs in the background. Settings › MyAnimeList shows "Up to date", "N changes waiting" or "Sending failed" with a **Retry** button.

**Contract:**
- The MAL section state gets `pendingCount` and `lastError`
- Action: `OnRetryClick`

**Acceptance:**
- A local outbox table. While connected, every add, edit and remove made on this device is queued.
- Changes pulled from our server are never queued, so another device's change is not sent twice (D17).
- A background sender sits behind an interface (WorkManager on Android) and runs with a network constraint and backoff. It uses `PATCH` and `DELETE` on `my_list_status`.
- Failed sends stay in the queue. Sending is idempotent.
- Tests with fakes for the scheduler and the MAL client.

**Depends on:** M2-13, M2-15.
**Out of scope:** getting changes from MAL (M2-22).

**Decisions** (made when the ticket was written; ask only if the code contradicts them):
- Strict D17: only changes made on this device while connected are queued. Nothing pulled from our server is queued, including changes from devices without MAL.
- On connect, app-only entries (not `on_mal`) are queued once (merge on connect).
- Remove in the app sends `DELETE` to MAL.
- WorkManager: a one-time job on each change (network constraint, exponential backoff) plus a 6-hour periodic retry. About 1 request per second through `MalThrottle`.
- Disconnect clears the queue.

title: Get changes made on MAL
body:
**Goal:** changes made on MyAnimeList's website come into the app.

**Where in the app:** this runs in the background. Settings › MyAnimeList also gets a **Sync now** button and a "last synced" time.

**Contract:**
- The MAL section state gets `lastSyncedAt` and `syncing`
- Action: `OnSyncNowClick`

**Acceptance:**
- A periodic background pull of the MAL list, reusing the reader from M2-20 and MAL's `updated_at`.
- A difference with no pending local change is applied, then synced to our server.
- A difference that has a pending local change becomes a conflict (M2-19).
- The user's choice is sent to MAL (M2-21) and to our server.
- Tests: no conflict, conflict, offline.

**Depends on:** M2-20, M2-21.
**Out of scope:** devices without MAL (M2-23).

**Decisions** (made when the ticket was written; ask only if the code contradicts them):
- Pull on app start (when the last pull is older than 15 minutes), every 6 hours with WorkManager, and from **Sync now**.
- An `on_mal` entry missing from the MAL list was removed on MAL. It is removed in the app, unless it has a pending local change; then it becomes a conflict.
- A choice the user makes is a local change, so M2-21 sends it to MAL.

title: MAL on a second device
body:
**Goal:** with the same Google account on several devices, a device without MyAnimeList knows what to do.

**Where in the app:** on a signed-in device that is not connected to MAL, while the account has MAL linked, a library banner and the Settings MAL section ask: **Connect MAL on this device** or **Not on this device**.

**Contract** (server first):
- SDL: `linkedPlatforms: [Platform!]!` on the account, plus mutations to link and unlink
- The MAL section state gets `linkedElsewhere`
- Actions: `OnConnectClick`, `OnNotOnThisDeviceClick`

**Acceptance:**
- The server stores only the platform name, no username or ID (D19). Flyway migration, SDL committed, server tests pass.
- Connecting MAL on any device sets the flag. Only **Unlink MAL from account** in Settings clears it.
- This device never sends changes pulled from our server to MAL (D17).
- The user's choice is remembered.
- Client tests.

**Order inside the ticket:** server and SDL first, then shared and composeApp in parallel.
**Depends on:** M2-22.
**Out of scope:** platforms other than MAL.

**Decisions** (made when the ticket was written; ask only if the code contradicts them):
- Strict D17: a device without MAL never sends anything to MAL. Its changes reach our server only, and the prompt says so.
- **Not on this device** is stored on the device and hides the prompt.
- Disconnecting on one device does not clear the server flag.

title: Server limits and input validation
body:
**Goal:** the public GraphQL endpoint resists abuse.

**Where in the app:** nowhere. Server only.

**Acceptance:**
- Query depth and complexity limits.
- A batch-size limit on `pushChanges` and a request size limit.
- Rate limits per user and per IP.
- Every input field validated (lengths, ranges, enums).
- The decision on introspection written down.
- A test for each limit. `server-tests` pass.

**Depends on:** nothing open. Can be done at any point.
**Out of scope:** hosting (M2-25).

**Decisions** (made when the ticket was written; ask only if the code contradicts them):
- Depth 10, complexity 1000. Push batch lowered from 1000 to 500, matching the pull page. Request body 256 KB.
- Ktor RateLimit: 60 per minute per user and 120 per minute per IP. Too many returns 429.
- Introspection is on in dev and off in production, decided by an env var.

title: Put the server online
body:
**Goal:** the release build of the app talks to our server on the internet over HTTPS.

**Acceptance:**
- An ADR compares at least three hosts (the mini PC from M2-28 and M2-30 is one of them) on price, HTTPS, Postgres backups and effort, with prices checked and dated. It picks one.
- The chosen host is set up: a production Docker image, migrations on start, JSON logs, a health check.
- Config is documented, with no secrets or private host details in the repo.
- A backup is restored once, to prove backups work.
- The release build points to the server URL.
- Deploy steps are in the README.

**Depends on:** M2-24.
**Out of scope:** CD automation, unless trivial.

**Decisions** (made when the ticket was written; ask only if the code contradicts them):
- The ADR compares the mini PC (behind an HTTPS tunnel) with at least two paid hosts, and the user picks.
- Without an own domain, use the host's or the tunnel's subdomain.
- Done before M2-27.

title: Privacy policy
body:
**Goal:** the privacy policy that Google Play and MyAnimeList require is public and reachable from the app.

**Where in the app:** Settings › **Privacy policy**, and a link in the MAL consent text (M2-15).

**Acceptance:**
- The page is at a public URL. It covers what our server stores (Google `sub`, library entries with anime IDs, the linked platform name), what stays on the device, MAL data and caching, deletion, and a contact for removal requests.
- A checklist in `docs/` against the MAL agreement: no stored credentials, cache only as needed, removal within 24 hours, no scraping, no revenue.
- The Settings row opens the page.

**Depends on:** nothing open. Can be done at any point. If M2-15 is done, add the link to its consent text.
**Out of scope:** legal review.

**Decisions** (made when the ticket was written; ask only if the code contradicts them):
- The page lives in the existing GitHub Pages repo, next to `assetlinks.json` and the account deletion page.
- Contact: a dedicated address the user creates and provides before the ticket starts. Stop and ask if it is missing.

title: Publish to Google Play internal testing
body:
**Goal:** the app is on the Google Play internal testing track.

**Acceptance:**
- A release build with R8. The keystore stays out of the repo.
- CI builds a signed AAB from secrets. `applicationId` and version are set.
- The target API level meets Play's current requirement (checked with a search).
- The Play App Signing SHA-256 is added to `/.well-known/assetlinks.json` in the Pages repo, and the MAL App Link is verified on a release build.
- Store listing, screenshots, the Data safety form, the account-deletion URL, the privacy policy URL and the content rating are done.
- The internal testing track is published.

**Depends on:** M2-25, M2-26.
**Out of scope:** production rollout.

**Decisions** (made when the ticket was written; ask only if the code contradicts them):
- Uses the user's existing Play developer account. `applicationId` stays `com.greenzean.animekmp`.
- The store listing text is drafted in the PR, for the user to approve before upload.

title: End-to-end check of the MVP
body:
**Goal:** prove the MVP works, starting from a clean install.

**Acceptance:**
- With no account: search, add, open details, track status, episodes and score, filter, export and import a file.
- Sign in with Google on two devices and see the same library.
- Connect MAL: import, change something on both sides, resolve a conflict, see the second-device prompt.
- Delete the account.
- The result goes in `docs/m2-result.md`, with every decision D1-D27 marked as met or listed as not met.
- CI, lint and tests pass on `main`.

**Depends on:** all other M2 tickets.
**Out of scope:** new features. Fixes go in bug tickets unless trivial.

**Decisions** (made when the ticket was written; ask only if the code contradicts them):
- None open.

title: Server: sign-out revokes the refresh token
body:
Goal: signing out also ends the session on the server, so a refresh token copied off the device stops working at once instead of after its 30 days.
Depends on: M2-4, M2-7.
Acceptance: a `signOut` mutation (authenticated by the refresh token) revokes the whole token family and returns a result that does not reveal whether the token existed; repeating it, or sending an unknown or already revoked token, is not an error; the SDL file and the schema drift test are updated and the Apollo operation is added; the app calls it during sign-out (after the keep-or-delete choice) and signs out locally even when the call fails or the device is offline; server tests cover revoke, repeat and a refresh with the revoked token (`UNAUTHENTICATED`); app tests cover the offline sign-out; ADR 0011 consequences and ADR 0010 are updated through a new ADR or a superseding note, not by rewriting an accepted one.
Out of scope: "sign out everywhere" (revoking every device's family), cleaning up expired token rows, rate limiting, changing the keep-or-delete behaviour.
Covers: follow-up to D20 (ADR 0011). Skill: graphql-schema, ktor-server-conventions.
Order: server schema first, then the app.

title: Mini PC runs everything except the apps; server and DB deploy after passing tests
body:
Goal: the Mac runs only the Android app, the emulator and Gradle builds; the server, PostgreSQL and Docker run on the mini PC. Server and DB changes are deployed to the mini PC automatically whenever the automated server tests pass, without asking.
Acceptance: `docker` and `docker compose` cannot run on the Mac from Claude Code sessions (the `docker compose *` and `docker info *` allow entries are removed from `.claude/settings.local.json` and a deny rule or hook blocks them); `scripts/dev-server.sh` no longer starts Postgres through local compose and targets the mini PC; a `server-deploy` script outside the repo (like `server-tests`) syncs the server build over SSH, applies the Flyway migrations, restarts the server and checks health; CLAUDE.md "Where things run" says that after `server-tests` passes, `server-deploy` runs without asking, and that no deploy runs when the tests fail or were not run; the Definition of Done in the `ticket-workflow` skill gets a "deployed and healthy" item for tickets that touch `server/`; a failed deploy is reported with its output and not retried silently; a new ADR (next free number) records the rule and is linked from `docs/decisions/README.md`; no host, address, user or key is in the repo.
Out of scope: production Dockerfile and hosting choice (M2-23, M2-24), a CI deploy job, exposing the server to the internet.
Covers: working rules in CLAUDE.md. Skill: ktor-server-conventions, postgres-migrations.
Order: settings and script first, then docs.
